Requesting changes for one issue: with this PR's defaults, video analysis fails out of the box.

`src/lib/adapters/video/videoAnalyzer.ts` now defaults to `gemini-3.8-flash` but keeps `DEFAULT_LOCATION = "us-central1"`. In a live check (details in https://github.com/juspay/neurolink/pull/2079#issuecomment-6387492218), `gemini-3.8-flash` returns 404 at `us-central1` and answers at `us` and `global`. Video analysis without `GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION` or `options.location` therefore hits that 404.

Suggested fix: resolve the video analyzer's location with `resolveVertexLocation(model, location)` from `src/lib/providers/googleVertex/client.ts`, the same helper the text path uses, which sends `gemini-*` to `global`. Defaulting it to `global` would also work. A test that checks the default location chosen for a Gemini model would keep this from coming back.

Re-checked 8efb947e1 against live Vertex today. The location problem from my earlier review is fixed.

I built the head and called `analyzeVideo`, `analyzeVideoWithVertexAI` and `executeVideoAnalysis` with the default model (`gemini-3.8-flash`) on a 3 s ffmpeg testsrc clip. The runs covered `GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION` unset and set to `us-central1`, plus the location options `us-central1` and `us`. All nine calls went to `/locations/global` and returned 200.

The new test covers `resolveVideoLocation` only, not that the call site uses it; the live run above covers that.

The head merges cleanly onto release 71dc84a. `test` and `security-suites` are red on GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f (`@hono/node-server`). Release itself fails `security-suites` on the same advisory, so that failure does not come from this PR. A fix is in progress separately.

Approving the code change.
